 New raw reports and hour aggregates record bounded `computation.version:3`: effective attribution policies/windows, per-slot reward/objective/decay tau, raw-day versus hourly-ring horizon/cap profile and the unweighted credited-outcome/item-decision unit. Carry-in-only credited slots are included even where the old arm projection has no denominator row. Day construction refuses unknown/mixed hourly bases or changed accumulator configuration before canonical replacement; estimator-only changes remain possible. Legacy saved days remain readable with unknown computation. Ambiguous duplicate-label custom reports preserve their existing response-only counts/grids but carry unknown computation. Valid basis survives full/paged diagnostics and the same-object summary. Windows expose per-slot `compatibility` status/reasons/dates and return no pooled arms for unknown, mixed or unrepresented contributions; this is withholding, not a zero result. The modern view shows these warnings. Equality establishes only recorded computation, not common served control/allocation/enrollment, metric/target versions, monetary outcomes or experimental compatibility. Objective/tau describe grids; arm credits remain unweighted repeated counts. There is no historical restamping/rebuild or policy choice. Older strict summary readers may reject the additive field; reader-first rollout requires separate qualification. Existing coverage, maturity, storage budgets and publication/history limitations remain. Version3 identifies current-input logical deduplication after version2 exact-reference attribution. Stored versions1/2 keep their labels and counts; mixed versions cannot be pooled.
 
-Raw/hourly readers compare complete logical records by tenant, stream and primary ID before distinct-row and ring caps. Exact decisions and validated nonce-bearing outcome retries count once; a changed payload or repeated nonce-free outcome ID refuses the report. Unique legacy outcomes remain supported. Only validated top-level `_ledger_delivery` transport provenance is excluded from equality. Optional `counts.duplicates:{decisions,outcomes}` records admitted repeats for the requested brand after erasure filtering and survives saved summaries; absence in an old report is unknown. This does not establish unique business orders or page views, online statistics idempotency, or complete delivery. Relevant ambiguous compact carry-in, including a forward input overlapping retained identity, refuses without repairing history; an already-folded-hour replay remains supported. Raw-input refusal precedes shard writes, but a later retained-shard failure can follow earlier shard progress, with no new hour aggregate published. Hourly full-record comparison now refuses above16MiB per object/combined physical UTF-8 text or1,000,000 admission work units. Retained-ID comparison across shards also has16MiB UTF-8 ID bytes and1,000,000 visited entries per build, with2048 bytes per relevant ID, checked before ring-cap projection. Physical object/byte/work caps still count duplicate traffic; these conservative application limits are not a supported customer envelope or deployed capacity proof.
+Raw/hourly readers compare complete logical records by tenant, stream and primary ID before distinct-row and ring caps. Exact decisions and validated nonce-bearing outcome retries count once; a changed payload or repeated nonce-free outcome ID refuses the report. Unique legacy outcomes remain supported. Only validated top-level `_ledger_delivery` transport provenance is excluded from equality. This does not establish unique business orders or page views, online statistics idempotency, or complete delivery. Relevant ambiguous compact carry-in, including a forward input overlapping retained identity, refuses without repairing history; an already-folded-hour replay remains supported. Hourly builds now validate all loaded shards and stage their complete numeric aggregate before any write, so a later retained-shard failure causes zero writes. Hourly full-record comparison refuses above16MiB per object/combined physical UTF-8 text or1,000,000 admission work units. Retained-ID comparison across shards also has16MiB UTF-8 ID bytes and1,000,000 visited entries per build, with2048 bytes per relevant ID, checked before ring-cap projection. Loaded and staged shard bodies each have a separate combined16MiB bound; the aggregate, complete coordinator and every possible partial-write mixture must fit the same bound. Physical object/byte/work caps still count duplicate traffic; these conservative application limits are not a supported customer envelope or deployed capacity proof.
 
-Strict raw-day reports and hourly folds refuse a selected, listed object that is unavailable; hourly malformed JSON also refuses before any shard, hour aggregate or canonical report write. Hourly raw and aggregate-inventory listings reject missing or repeated continuation cursors and bound page/key visits by the existing1,000,000 work ceiling. Valid pagination, empty hours and explicit physical-cap truncation remain supported. A still-pending hour can retry after its input is restored, within the existing catch-up lookback and horizon. Catch-up continues after failures, so later progress can lose earlier carry-in; restoring an earlier input does not rebuild later hours or repair existing partial aggregates. General non-strict `loadDay` callers retain legacy missing-object/malformed-line skipping. This is input refusal and bounded retry, not complete late-arrival or pipeline recovery.
+Strict raw-day reports and hourly folds refuse a selected, listed object that is unavailable; hourly malformed JSON also refuses before any shard, hour aggregate or canonical report write. Hourly raw and aggregate-inventory listings reject missing or repeated continuation cursors and bound page/key visits by the existing1,000,000 work ceiling. Valid pagination, empty hours and explicit physical-cap truncation remain supported. Before shard progress, the existing shard-zero object conditionally stores the exact prepared aggregate, original publication condition and before/after shard fingerprints. Restarted retries preserve its credits, counters, `builtAt` and `ringsFolded`, including carry-in evicted by partial progress. Complete selected raw bytes, observed inventory/cap, effective fold configuration and sorted visitor/erasure-cutoff pairs must match; unrelated erasure rewrite progress does not invalidate that basis. Unknown or changed state refuses before further recovery writes. Every mutation uses an ETag/absence condition; uncertain acknowledgement permits only bounded exact-byte readback. Changed shards and aggregates retain a unique technical `generation` marker to prevent stale writers reusing older ETags; this is separate from computation-policy versions. No additional visitor history or storage namespace is introduced. These fingerprints bind observed inputs, not an atomic snapshot across raw objects and erasure stores. Changed pending input/configuration/erasure requires separate recovery; it is not a rule declaring delayed events invalid. Completed explicit same/older-hour recomputation retains its existing surviving-history and erasure-cleanup limits. No new event-age cutoff, historical reconstruction, dependent-hour repair or old-binary coordination is promised; retain compatible readers/writers until pending checkpoints drain. General non-strict `loadDay` callers retain legacy missing-object/malformed-line skipping.
 
-The five-minute catch-up also retries missing or stale canonical day publication after successful hours, even when no new hour is folded. It checks the newest three aggregate-backed dates in its lookback, oldest first, and reports published/failed/deferred date counts separately from pending hours. A saved aggregate summary skips publication only when its built-hour set matches the complete date inventory; read failures never permit replacement. Retries use current aggregates without raw fallback or refolding. Matching hour membership does not detect changed aggregate contents, configuration/erasure freshness or newly closed missing hours. Dates outside the lookback or deferred by a longer custom lookback, concurrent publication fencing and historical reconstruction remain separate recovery work. Ordinary report requests retain best-effort persistence; a returned computation does not prove a saved write.
+The five-minute catch-up first checks shard zero for an interrupted transaction, including one whose aggregate already exists or whose hour has left the lookback. It recovers that transaction under the same hour/budget limits before newer hours; unresolved work stops newer folds, and `maxHours:0` performs no fold recovery writes. Pending counts include that debt once, alongside missing hours. Added recovery/storage calls count against the fold budget, which admits a started fold rather than proving a per-invocation capacity limit. Pre-transaction failures retain bounded skip behavior and do not reconstruct lost carry-in. Catch-up also retries missing or stale canonical day publication after successful hours, even when no new hour is folded. It checks the newest three aggregate-backed dates in its lookback, oldest first, and reports published/failed/deferred date counts separately from pending hours. A recovered date outside that lookback is explicitly deferred. A saved aggregate summary skips publication only when its built-hour set matches the complete date inventory; read failures never permit replacement. Retries use current aggregates without raw fallback or refolding, and a true no-op changes no stored bytes. Matching hour membership does not detect changed aggregate contents, configuration/erasure freshness or newly closed missing hours. Deferred dates, concurrent day-publication fencing and historical reconstruction remain separate recovery work. Ordinary report requests retain best-effort persistence; a returned computation does not prove a saved write.
 
 Raw reports admit at most50,000 distinct decisions and50,000 distinct outcomes,6 policies including learning (the existing4 presets plus1 custom fit),800 raw ledger objects,16MiB per object and combined raw UTF-8 text,1,000,000 estimated work units,16,384 projected item/slot/ancestor cells across policies, and8MiB final report JSON. Work includes ring construction/sorting, policy/outcome filtering/sorting and featured-product cross-products; listing traversal is also bounded. Consumed components are limited to256 UTF-8 bytes and generated keys to2048 bytes; invalid shapes or inherited object-property names return400. Capacity refusal returns no-store413 with `code:report_budget_exceeded`, `budget`, `limit` and `observed`, before any partial raw publication; object refusals retain `objects`/`max`. General capped loader callers retain their separate truncation contract. Native object size and actual stream bytes are checked; text-only adapters can check actual bytes only after materialization. These are application safety budgets, not proved Worker CPU/memory, supported customer traffic or scientific policy limits.
